key_insight: Vision-language models' visual reasoning can be used to propose and evaluate macro placements, and when integrated into an evolutionary optimizer (VeoPlace) they produce higher-quality floorplans than optimization or ML-only approaches.
problem_solved: Automating the combinatorial, spatially-complex task of macro placement in chip floorplanning by incorporating human-like visual reasoning to guide layout generation and refinement.
method: Encode the chip canvas and candidate placements as visual inputs to a vision-language model to obtain spatial assessments and placement proposals.
Integrate VLM evaluations/proposals into an evolutionary optimization loop that generates, scores, and mutates macro placements under physical and routing constraints.
Combine VLM-derived spatial scores with traditional EDA objectives (e.g., wirelength, congestion) to form a composite fitness used for selection and refinement.
impact: Introduces a multimodal toolchain that brings visual reasoning to a core EDA problem, enabling more automated, interpretable, and effective macro placement—reducing manual effort and accelerating design iterations for AI/ML hardware teams.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing: floorplan image → VLM scoring/proposal → evolutionary optimizer → final placement
Before/after floorplan comparison highlighting improved macro arrangement and reduced congestion
Fitness-over-generations chart illustrating convergence and improvement versus baselines
Heatmap or attention overlay from the VLM showing regions driving placement decisions
paper_title: See it to Place it: Evolving Macro Placements with Vision-Language Models
paper_authors: Ikechukwu Uchendu, Swati Goel, Karly Hou, Ebrahim Songhori, Kuang-Huei Lee
